title: VaultTec — Phase 4b Mean-Reversion Follow-Up Report
method: Out-of-sample test of the Bollinger and RSI mean-reversion hypothesis from Phase 4: three earlier, non-overlapping 180-calendar-day windows ending before the Phase 4 window starts, delayed real market history from yfinance (free), 40 days of warm-up history before each window. Two variants per strategy per window — A: risk-managed validation (3% stop / 4.5% target / 10-day exit through the Risk Engine, $10,000 virtual cash, balanced profile, long-only); B: native backtest exactly as in backtest.py (RSI sell > 70, Bollinger sell at upper band, no fixed stop/target). Signals use history up to the trade day only — no look-ahead. The Phase 4 window is re-run and labelled in-sample.
data_source: yfinance (delayed real market data, free — Yahoo Finance)

note: Out-of-sample results are the honest test of the mean-reversion hypothesis: the strategies were picked because they looked good on the Phase 4 window, so that window cannot confirm them. A result that holds across all three earlier windows would support further testing; a result that fades or reverses means the Phase 4 backtest numbers were a one-window artefact. Nothing here proves future profits: past performance does not guarantee future results, and live paper trades over real days plus a compliance/legal review are still required before any real money is considered. Method note: the in-sample native backtests here start at row 60 of each history (the validation warm-up), while Phase 4's backtest suite ran on the full history — so in-sample trade counts here (RSI 10, Bollinger 10) are lower than Phase 4's (20, 24); mean returns are still directly comparable.
